newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line says price war hits 9-mo.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line says price war hits 9-mo.

text.p: Swedish ferry operator Stena Line on Thursday blamed a price war over the English Channel for a loss for the first nine months of the year, repeating its full-year forecast for a loss of around 450 million crowns.
Stena Line posted a loss of 251 million crowns ($38.3 million) for the nine months ending September 30, compared to a profit of 272 million crowns in the corresponding period a year ago.
"The deterioration in profits ... is due to comprehensive tonnage reallocations resulting from delays in ship deliveries and associated running in problems," Stena said in a statement.

"Operational disruptions and the competitive situation in the English Channel have led to the group's profit ... for the third quarter, i.e. the peak season months from July to September, being cut by more than half."
Profit after financial items was slashed to 309 million crowns in the third quarter from 622 million a year ago.
Stena Line's sales during the nine months fell by 6.5 percent to 7.07 billion crowns. ($ = 6.552 Swedish Crowns)
